note: Media Download has no configure route (configure=null), no settings, no schema, no permissions, no Drush and no plugins. It replaces core's entity.media.canonical route with DownloadController::save so /media/{id} serves the source file (inline, or ?dl=1 for attachment), forces media.settings:standalone_url TRUE via a config.factory.override, and denies page-caching of binary responses. Evals are grounded in that: recipe questions cover the URL/route/override; introspection reads the effective overridden config and the canonical route controller on the live site; execution creates a document media entity and verifies its /media/{id} response via an internal http_kernel sub-request run as uid 1 (needs 'view media'). Fixtures use namespaced media named mdl_* and are deleted on cleanup/reset.

evals.prompt: With the media_download module enabled, what URL downloads a media entity's file, and how do I make the browser force a 'Save as' download rather than displaying the file inline?
evals.expected_output: Visit the media's canonical path /media/{id}: by default it serves the file inline (Content-Disposition: inline). Append ?dl=1 (i.e. /media/{id}?dl=1) to force an attachment download. DownloadController::save() sets attachment when the request query dl === '1'.

evals.prompt: Media Download's canonical /media/{id} URLs depend on core Media's 'standalone media URL' setting. What does the module do about that setting, and can I turn it off on the media settings form while the module is installed?
evals.expected_output: It ships a config.factory.override (MediaSettingsOverride) that forces media.settings:standalone_url to TRUE at runtime, so the effective value is always TRUE regardless of the stored value. The media settings form shows a warning that changing the toggle has no effect while Media Download is installed.

evals.prompt: How does media_download change what happens when you visit a media entity's canonical page? Name the route it alters and the controller that now handles it.
evals.expected_output: RouteSubscriber removes core's entity.media.canonical route and re-registers /media/{media} pointing at Drupal\media_download\DownloadController::save (requirement _entity_access: media.view). So the canonical page returns the file instead of the rendered media entity page.

evals.prompt: On this running Drupal site, what is the EFFECTIVE value of media.settings standalone_url as seen by the application, and which module is responsible for that value? Note the stored config value may differ from the effective one.
evals.expected_output: The effective value \Drupal::config('media.settings')->get('standalone_url') is TRUE, forced by media_download's MediaSettingsOverride (a config.factory.override), even though the stored value (getEditable) may be FALSE.

evals.prompt: This site has a document media entity named 'mdl_known'. If a user with access visits that media's canonical /media/{id} page, will they see a rendered media page or a file download, and which controller handles it? Inspect the running site's routing to answer.
evals.expected_output: They get a direct file download/response, not the rendered media page: the entity.media.canonical route (/media/{media}) is handled by Drupal\media_download\DownloadController::save. Inspect with e.g. drush php:eval reading \Drupal::service('router.route_provider')->getRouteByName('entity.media.canonical')->getDefault('_controller').

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site (media_download is installed), create a Media entity of type 'document' named 'mdl_task' whose source field references a real file that exists on disk, so that the media's canonical path /media/{id} serves that file directly as a download. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A document media named 'mdl_task' exists with field_media_document referencing an on-disk file; requesting /media/{id} (as a user with 'view media') returns HTTP 200 with a Drupal\media_download\CacheableBinaryFileResponse (Content-Disposition: inline), served by DownloadController.

evals.prompt: On this site, create a downloadable 'document' Media entity named 'mdl_dl' (source field referencing a real on-disk file) such that visiting /media/{id}?dl=1 forces the browser to save the file (attachment), while /media/{id} shows it inline. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A document media named 'mdl_dl' exists referencing an on-disk file; via media_download's DownloadController /media/{id}?dl=1 returns Content-Disposition: attachment and /media/{id} returns inline (HTTP 200). No module code change is needed - the ?dl=1 behaviour is built in.
